chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Ziyād ibn Marwān al-Qandī—and he was from the Waqifites—who said:

I entered upon Abū Ibrāhīm, and with him was his son Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. So he said to me: “O Ziyād, this is my son so-and-so. His document is my document, his speech is my speech, his messenger is my messenger, and whatever he says, then the word is his word.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the son identified and designated in the report
key_terms.أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abū Ibrāhīm, the Imam speaking in the narration
key_terms.رَسُولُهُ: his envoy or messenger, acting with delegated authority
key_terms.كَلَامُهُ: his speech, presented as fully representative
key_terms.كِتَابُهُ: his written communication or letter, carrying authoritative force

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the authority of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام after Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abū Ibrāhīm's designation of his son Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام and affirms the son's religious authority as an extension of his own. The wording emphasizes continuity of Imamate, indicating that his son's written communication, speech, and representation carry the same binding authority.
